# Choose the article’s shape

Choose by the reader’s intended outcome. An incident may illustrate an explainer or support an argument. It earns a separate article only when it answers a second question.

| Genre | What the reader came for | What earns the conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Incident or method | Diagnose a similar failure or reuse the method that exposed it. | Open with the observable symptom. Reconstruct the sequence from evidence, show the discriminating check and give the reader a way to verify the repair. Separate observed events from a proposed explanation. |
| Technical explainer | Understand a mechanism well enough to predict its behavior. | Introduce the problem and trace one input to an observable result. Change a condition and show where the explanation stops applying. Distinguish an illustrative trace from a measurement. |
| Thought leadership | Decide whether to change a belief or practice. | State a contestable claim, present the strongest plausible alternative and identify evidence that distinguishes them. Say when the alternative wins. |
| Tooling update | Decide whether to adopt, upgrade or migrate. | Demonstrate the change on a real task. State availability, prerequisites, migration cost and limits. For a retirement, say what happens to existing users and what replaces the capability. |
| How-to | Complete and verify a task. | Show the starting state, prerequisites, steps and expected observations. Run the complete path before describing it as verified. Include a recovery route for a failure actually encountered. |
| Bench report | Choose between alternatives under stated conditions. | Describe the workload, selection criteria, baseline and measures. Compare like with like, report exceptions and show which changed constraint could reverse the choice. |
| Research note | Understand a new hypothesis and how to test it. | Identify the prior result, proposed mechanism, evidence so far and competing explanations. Specify an observation that would count against the idea. Separate open questions from findings. |

For a series, give each installment an outcome a reader can reach on its own. Link to an earlier installment for a genuine prerequisite and tell the reader what knowledge it supplies.
